title: How Much of the Statutory Tax Comes Back on a Hotel Rate Plans Cancellation
content:
The share of the tax element returned on a cancellation settlement against a Hotel Rate Plans reservation turns on whether the arrival date has passed and on the form in which the rate plan booked returns value.

## Determining the share returned

1. Where the arrival date has not passed and the rate plan booked returns value to the original form of payment, 100 percent of the tax element is returned.
2. Where the arrival date has passed and the rate plan booked returns value to the original form of payment, 0 percent of the tax element is returned.
3. In every other case 0 percent of the tax element is returned.

The arrival date has not passed while the handling date is on or before it; it has passed once the handling date falls after it. A reservation handled on the arrival date itself is one whose arrival date has not passed.

## The cases the determination covers

| Arrival date | Plan returns value to the original form of payment | Share of the tax element returned |
| --- | --- | --- |
| not passed | yes | 100 percent |
| passed | yes | 0 percent |
| not passed | no | 0 percent |
| passed | no | 0 percent |

The only case that returns any of the tax element at all is the first.

## Illustration on hypothetical figures

A tax element of 132.00 USD, being the occupancy tax and the city tax posted on the reservation taken together:

- Handled 6 days before arrival on the Semi-Flexible Rate, which returns value to the original form of payment, the tax returned is 100 percent of 132.00 USD, which is 132.00 USD.
- Handled on the arrival date itself on that plan, the arrival date has not passed, and the tax returned is again 132.00 USD.
- Handled 1 day after arrival on that plan, the tax returned is 0 percent of 132.00 USD, which is 0.00 USD.
- Handled at any time on the All-Inclusive Flex Rate, which returns value as credit at the property, the tax returned is 0.00 USD.
